hypothesis: hyperparameter_capacity is the one lever category never actually tried on the accepted-best plain bilinear BPR-FM: `k` (embedding/interaction dimension) is hardcoded at 16 and was never itself swept (only L2, dropout-on-a-different-architecture, aux-loss-weight, ensemble-weight, and rare-id-collapse-threshold have been swept so far). While I'm at it, I'm fixing a latent robustness bug in `run_model`: it currently does `run_fm(splits, seed=seed, verbose=verbose, **hparams)`, which would raise `TypeError` if the harness's generic hparams dict ever contains a key `run_fm` doesn't accept — I'm switching to explicit `hparams.get(name, default)` reads per the harness contract, with no change to the underlying FM/BPR mechanism itself.
reflection: The requested EDA round mostly resurfaced fields (author-level aggregates, user_active_degree, tag, upload_type) whose mechanism (naive field-widening) was already directly falsified twice by the project's own ablation under both loss functions — retrying them without a different encoding/architecture wouldn't be a genuinely new test. Meanwhile the noise-floor probe (node 13) shows primary's bootstrap std (~0.0017, 90% range ~0.0055) is comparable to or larger than nearly every accepted/rejected gap seen so far (0.6041 vs 0.6033-0.6037), which is the more likely explanation for the plateau than any single rejected mechanism being wrong.
expected_effect: I expect GAUC to move more than nDCG@5, since embedding capacity affects the quality of pairwise bilinear interactions used across the full eligible-user comparison pool (what GAUC aggregates), whereas nDCG@5 is dominated by noise from the majority of valid users who have fewer than 5 rows.
